dominant_strengths: Clear semantic color coding for toast variants (green/blue/yellow/red) maps cleanly to user expectations of severity.
Notification cards use icon + title + body hierarchy with progress bars indicating auto-dismiss timing — functional and legible.
Dark backdrop allows colored accents and progress bars to pop with reasonable contrast for quick scanning.
dominant_weaknesses: Layout is generic Tailwind-toast convention — no distinguishing motion, stacking choreography, or compositional voice differentiates it.
Trigger buttons float in dead center of a vast empty canvas, creating awkward spatial composition disconnected from the corner stack.
Typography is serviceable but flat: identical weight/scale across all toasts, no rhythm between title and supporting copy beyond color.
fix_priorities: Introduce stacking motion language (slide-in, gentle scale, peek behind) so the stack feels alive rather than statically pinned.
Tighten card internals — increase title/body contrast in size or weight, refine icon container padding for crisper craft.
Replace centered button row with a contextual demo frame or hide controls so the notification stack is the hero element.
Unify accent border-left treatment across all four toast types for a coherent system signature.
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral utility leads via clear semantic colors and dismiss affordances, but visceral polish and reflective memorability remain generic.
rationale.intent_fit: It does deliver a working notification stack, but it reads as a default component-library demo rather than an authored design moment.
